inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 is FY2026E (US$3,684.6m = FY2025 actual US$3,411.6m x 1.08; H1 FY2026 actual +10.7% YoY to US$1,842.1m, H2 assumed softer as intra-Asia spot rates eased from July). The forecast horizon is FY2027-FY2036. FY0 is set to the current year rather than the last reported year so that the net-cash anchor and the flows do not overlap: FY2026 cash generation has already been largely distributed to earlier holders (US$587m dividends paid H1 2026, US$518m interim paid 15 Sept 2026). Using FY2025 as FY0 with the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet would count H1 2026 FCF twice and would ignore the September interim, overstating value by roughly US$1bn (about HK$2.8/share).
inputs.share_count_basis: Shares in issue at 30 June 2026: 2,699,988,016 in issue at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR note 31) scaled by the growth in issued share capital (US$34,954k / US$34,806k, H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet) = 2,711.5m. Includes ~34m shares held under the share award scheme, which the EPS table treats as dilutive and which will vest to employees; SBC is fully expensed in the flows so the count is held FLAT. Cross-check: H1 FY2026 diluted weighted average 2,703,494,712 (0.3% lower).
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, unaudited): cash and cash equivalents US$212.2m + time deposits with original maturity over three months US$720.2m = US$932.4m; interest-bearing bank loans US$33.1m. Lease liabilities (US$294.3m) are EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B) - the full lease cash cost is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Trade payables are operating, not debt. Financial assets at FVTPL (US$73.7m) and NCI (US$26.3m) are in equity_bridge. Roll-forward of this 30-Jun-2026 position to the FY0 (31 Dec 2026) year-end is also in equity_bridge: minus the HK$1.50 interim dividend paid 15 Sept 2026, plus H2 FY2026E owner FCF.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 actual, US$m: reported FCF 1,265.7 (OCF 1,401.0 - capex 135.3) - SBC 27.0 - bank interest / investment income / FV gains 37.8 - lease cash 89.5 (principal 77.9 + interest 11.6) = 1,111.4 owner FCF under lease treatment (B). The lease deduction is the extension of the standard identity required when lease liabilities are kept out of net debt. FY2026E owner FCF on the same basis is ~US$1,181m (H1 FY2026 actual 562.7).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 income statement line 'Bank interest income, other investment income and fair value gains on financial assets' US$37,831k (FY2024: 27,027k). The whole non-operating line is stripped because its source assets (US$932.4m cash + time deposits, US$73.7m FVTPL assets) are added in the bridge. Net cash is 0.8x owner FCF, below the 1x rule of thumb, but the double-count logic applies at any ratio once the cash is in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated statement of cash flows, 'Share award expense' US$26,952k (FY2024: 27,829k), note 8. Equity-settled awarded shares; no cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes equals the add-back.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases US$0.9m (H1 FY2026: US$3.9m). The flat share count is a modelling convention the company funds only partially; awarded shares are mostly newly issued (issued capital rose 0.4% in H1 FY2026), so the ~0.8%-of-revenue SBC charge in the flows is the full cost of that dilution.
inputs.fx_note: USD/HKD 7.8476 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-16). Statements, flows, WACC and all per-share values are built in USD and converted to HKD at this rate for comparison with the HKEX quote. HKD is pegged to USD in a 7.75-7.85 band under the Linked Exchange Rate System, so the conversion carries at most +/-0.6% of FX risk; there is no dual listing to parity-check, the peg band is the check (7.8476 sits inside it). Direction: USD per-share value x 7.8476 = HKD per-share value.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD so WACC is USD-built: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 for a HK-listed container line = cost of equity ~10%; net cash, so WACC = cost of equity = 10.0%. No ad-hoc cyclicality or governance premium and no per-scenario WACC differences: cyclicality is charged once, in the flows, through the bear scenario's weight (30%) and the trough-margin paths. Terminal growth 2.5% (USD nominal, below long-run intra-Asia trade growth). Terminal cap 12x owner FCF in the base (10x bear, 14x bull) - the 12-15x cyclical cap of the method, set at the low end because listed container lines rarely sustain double-digit FCF multiples at mid-cycle; the cap binds in the base and bear; in the bull the 14x cap sits above Gordon (13.7x at 10%/2.5%), so Gordon binds there.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. SITC charters 20-21 of its ~120 vessels (IFRS 16 lease liabilities US$294.3m at 30 June 2026). The full lease cash cost - principal (FY2025 US$77.9m, financing) plus interest on lease liabilities (US$11.6m) = US$89.5m = 2.6% of revenue - is deducted inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is therefore ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 depreciation of PP&E US$116.0m (3.4% of revenue), excluding ROU depreciation of US$64.2m. EBITDA margin anchors are on the reported IFRS-16 basis (pre-lease), so the lease line is not double counted. The lease charge glides from 2.6% to 2.0% as owned newbuild deliveries (US$763m committed at 30 June 2026) replace chartered tonnage; capex and D&A rise correspondingly.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests (US$26.3m at 30 June 2026, ~1% of equity) are deducted once, in equity_bridge. FY2025 NCI share of profit was US$7.5m on US$1,230m - immaterial to the margin anchor.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (USD flows vs HKD quote, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for the stripped investment income, risk charged once). SITC is an operating company - an intra-Asia container carrier with ~10% logistics revenue - so the owner-FCF engine is the right model; none of the non-FCF routes apply. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). EBITDA ANCHOR: FY2025 segment results US$1,229.0m + depreciation US$180.2m (incl. ROU) = US$1,409.2m = 41.3% of revenue on an operating basis that already excludes interest/FV income and finance costs; it includes US$45.0m of other income and gains (mainly gains on disposal of 3 vessels; FY2024 US$18.0m), so the normalised FY2025 operating EBITDA margin is ~40.6%. FY2026E is run at 41.0% (H1 FY2026 net margin 36.7% implies ~42%; H2 softer). CYCLE: this is a peak-earnings year. Average freight rate (ex slot exchange) was ~US$1,093/TEU in FY2022, US$623 at the FY2023 trough, US$721 in FY2024, US$753 in FY2025 and still rising YoY in H1 FY2026 on Red Sea diversions and a thin 2026 intra-Asia delivery schedule; volume grew 3.22m -> 3.85m TEU FY2023-FY2025 (+7.8% in both FY2025 and H1 FY2026). Operating EBITDA margins were 29.3% (FY2020), 44.2%, 51.9%, 30.1% (FY2023 trough), 40.3%, 41.3%: the ex-super-cycle average is ~35%, and the owned-fleet share has risen (99 of 119 vessels at FY2025), which lifts trough margins versus 2020/2023. The BASE therefore normalises rather than extrapolates: revenue -8% in FY2027 (rate ~US$690/TEU, volume +4%) and flat in FY2028 (rate ~US$665), then mid-cycle volume growth of 3-4% fading to 2.5%; operating EBITDA margin steps down from 41% to a 34% mid-cycle level by FY2030 and stays there. Capex follows the committed orderbook (US$763m of vessels contracted at 30 June 2026 for 2027-2029 delivery, plus containers) at 8.5% of revenue in FY2027-28 before settling at 5.5% (above D&A ex-ROU of ~4.3%, i.e. continuing fleet growth at today's newbuild prices). CASH TAX: FY2025 income tax US$20.9m on PBT US$1,251m (1.7%), cash taxes paid US$22.8m. This is structural, not a one-off shelter: international shipping income is exempt in Hong Kong (IRO s.23B) and under PRC/treaty rules, and is carved out of the OECD Pillar Two GloBE rules. The base ramps from 2.0% to 3.0% of EBIT as the (taxable) land-logistics mix grows; the bear takes it to 5%. TIMING: FY0 = FY2026E and the 30-Jun-2026 net cash is rolled to 31 Dec 2026 in equity_bridge (see base_revenue_note and net_debt_note). Year-1 (FY2027) flows are discounted a full year from October 2026 - slightly conservative - against which the Dec-2026 cash is taken undiscounted; the two roughly offset. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported alongside; SBC is only 0.8% of revenue so the house/street band is narrow.
inputs.fleet_note: FY2025: 119 vessels (99 owned 162,444 TEU + 20 chartered 22,517 TEU), 184,961 TEU total; 120 vessels at 30 June 2026. Capital commitments for vessels US$763.3m at 30 June 2026 (US$909.1m at 31 Dec 2025), contracted but not provided; options for 8 further vessels (~US$213m) exercised Jan/Mar 2026; depot commitments US$2.8m.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 4.8% vs revenue 3yr -6.0% and EPS 3yr -14.5%; equity 5yr 15.9% vs EPS 5yr 28.0%. Every CAGR here is cycle-phase dependent: FY2020 and FY2023 are troughs, FY2022 and FY2025 are peaks, so the 5-year figures measure trough-to-peak and the 3-year figures peak-to-peak. None is a forward anchor; the selected 3.0% is mid-cycle intra-Asia volume growth net of freight-rate normalisation.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest/investment income - lease principal and interest), US$m: FY2020 243.3, FY2021 1,067.9, FY2022 1,394.8, FY2023 231.2, FY2024 772.5, FY2025 1,111.4 (lease interest for FY2020-21 estimated at ~US$6-8m; FY2022-25 read from the filings). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 35.5% vs reported 32.1%: the gap is the interest income on a growing cash pile (US$9m -> US$38m) and lease cash (US$55m -> US$90m), not SBC, which is flat at ~US$27m. Equity CAGR is depressed by the payout: dividends paid FY2021-FY2025 total US$4.37bn against US$5.89bn of net income.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle normalisation from a peak year. FY2027 revenue -8% as the average freight rate eases from ~US$780/TEU to ~US$690 (still 11% above the FY2023 trough of US$623) while volume grows ~4%; FY2028 flat (rate ~US$665, volume +4%); then 3-4% volume-led growth fading to 2.5%. Operating EBITDA margin steps 41% -> 35.5% -> 33% and settles at 34% mid-cycle, above the 29-30% troughs of FY2020/FY2023 because 99 of 119 vessels are now owned at low entry prices. Capex 8.5% of revenue in FY2027-28 honours the US$763m committed orderbook, then 5.5%. Cash tax 2% -> 3%, structural shipping exemption retained. WC capture 2% (net payables ~2.3% of revenue; a revenue fall consumes cash).

bull.narrative: No rate normalisation: Red Sea diversions persist, the intra-Asia delivery schedule stays thin, and China+1 relocation plus India/Southeast Asia network additions keep volume at +5% with rates holding ~US$750-780/TEU. Revenue compounds 5% for four years then fades to 3%. Operating EBITDA margin holds 39% (slightly below the FY2025-26 peak as bunker and port costs inflate) on the owned-fleet cost advantage. Capex stays elevated (8% -> 6%) because the company keeps buying vessels to match volume growth. Shipping tax exemption intact at 2%. Terminal cap 14x. This is roughly what today's price discounts.

bear.narrative: Down-cycle on the FY2023 pattern but deeper: the Red Sea reopens in 2027, the >7m TEU global orderbook pushes redeployed tonnage into intra-Asia, and US tariff escalation slows China-linked volumes to +2%. The average rate falls to ~US$580/TEU (below the FY2023 trough, roughly FY2019's US$520 inflated), so revenue -18% then -6%. Operating EBITDA margin troughs at 23% (FY2023 was 30% but on a smaller committed orderbook and lower cost base), recovers only to 29%. The US$763m of committed newbuilds is paid regardless, so capex is 10% of a shrinking revenue base in FY2027-28; D&A and lease costs are sticky in dollars. Tax drifts to 5% as logistics mix grows and exemption scrutiny rises. Terminal cap 10x. Net cash and zero gearing mean this is a valuation event, not a solvency one.

scenario_narratives.base: Normalisation, not extrapolation. SITC is at or near peak earnings (FY2025 ROE 50%, average freight rate US$753/TEU vs the US$623 trough two years earlier), and the base assumes rates give back about half the FY2023-26 gain over FY2027-28 while volume keeps compounding at 4%. Operating EBITDA settles at a 34% mid-cycle margin - above the 29-30% troughs of FY2020 and FY2023 because the fleet is now 83% owned at counter-cyclical prices, below the 40-42% of FY2024-26 which carried a Red Sea rate tailwind. The US$763m committed orderbook is paid out in FY2027-29 and lifts owned capacity, so lease costs fall and D&A rises. Owner FCF troughs at ~US$700m in FY2028 and recovers to ~US$1.05bn by FY2036, about where it is today - i.e. ten years of volume growth are needed just to replace the rate cycle. Terminal value at the 12x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The current rate environment is the new normal. Red Sea disruption, thin intra-Asia deliveries and China+1 relocation keep rates near US$750-780/TEU, volume compounds 5% a year, and the owned-fleet cost advantage holds the operating EBITDA margin at ~39%. Owner FCF grows from ~US$1.2bn to ~US$1.65bn by FY2036 and is capitalised at 14x. This scenario roughly reproduces the current market price, which is why it carries only 20%: it needs rates, volume and costs all to hold at once in an industry whose rates fell 43% in a single year three years ago.
scenario_narratives.bear: A FY2023-style down-cycle arriving on top of a committed capex programme. Red Sea reopening and global orderbook deliveries push rates to ~US$580/TEU, tariffs slow China-linked volumes, and revenue falls 23% over two years while the US$763m of newbuilds still has to be paid for. Owner FCF falls to ~US$270m in FY2028 and recovers only to ~US$630m by FY2036 as the margin settles at 29%. Even here the balance sheet (US$0.9bn net cash, 0% gearing) is never stressed - the risk is to the valuation, not to the company. Terminal value at a 10x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 30/50/20. Bear up to 30%: the business is at a cyclical earnings peak (freight rates and ROE both at post-super-cycle highs), the Red Sea tailwind is a geopolitical accident that can reverse on a single announcement, the global orderbook is the largest since 2008, and intra-Asia spot indices have already softened since July 2026 - a sharp down-year in 2027 is a mainstream outcome, not a tail. Bull down to 20%: it requires rates, volume growth and cost discipline to hold simultaneously for a decade, and it is roughly what the current price already discounts. Base 50%: mid-cycle normalisation is the central case. No going-concern or covenant element in any scenario (net cash, 0% gearing).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a cyclical on normalised mid-cycle owner FCF, never on the peak year. SITC is an excellent operator - the lowest-cost pure intra-Asia carrier, 83% owned fleet bought counter-cyclically, net cash, 50% ROE at the top of the cycle, and a payout that returned US$4.4bn in five years - but freight rates are a commodity price it does not set. The model charges the cycle once, in the flows: a 30% bear weight, a base case that gives back half the FY2023-26 rate gain, and a terminal cap of 10-14x owner FCF. It charges leases once (treatment B, inside EBITDA, liabilities out of net debt), SBC once (expensed, count flat), the cash pile once (interest and FV income stripped, cash and FVTPL assets in the bridge) and timing once (FY0 = FY2026E; the September interim dividend removed from the 30-Jun cash, H2 FCF added back). The structural shipping tax exemption is retained because it is statutory and carved out of Pillar Two, not an NOL that expires. Street basis differs from house by only the ~0.8% SBC charge.
key_risks_to_valuation: Freight-rate path: every 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin is worth roughly US$0.10 (HK$0.8) per share; the base's 34% could be 30% if the owned-fleet advantage does not lift trough margins as assumed
Red Sea reopening or a tariff-driven volume shock would make the bear path the base path for FY2027-28
Capex: management buys vessels opportunistically and may exercise further options; capex above the modelled 5.5-8.5% of revenue lowers owner FCF unless it also lifts volume
Tax: loss of the international shipping exemption (HK IRO s.23B, Pillar Two carve-out) would move the cash tax rate from ~2-3% toward 15%+, worth roughly 12-15% of value
Terminal cap: at 12x owner FCF the terminal value is ~45% of EV; the market has at times paid under 8x for container lines at mid-cycle
Governance: 40.7% family control with related-party chartering carved out of the non-competition deed; no FX hedging on RMB/JPY exposures
FX: HKD peg gives +/-0.6% translation risk; a peg break would move the HKD values one-for-one
